speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis

Based on your history of a prior ant bite, the one-month duration of the lesion starting as a red spot and enlarging, combined with your immunocompromised state due to Crohn's disease and diabetes, I suspect a parasitic infection. Can you confirm if the lesion is currently weeping, crusting, or has raised borders, and does it hurt more at night?
